newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Mahathir says Malaysia negotiating Fokker rescue.
newsitem.headline: Mahathir says Malaysia negotiating Fokker rescue.

text.p: Malaysian Prime Minister Mahathir Mohamad said the government is involved in negotiations to rescue bankrupt Dutch aircraft maker Fokker NV, local newspapers reported on Thursday.
"We are looking at it. If it is feasible and viable, yes," Mahathir was quoted as saying by Business Times daily in response to questions from reporters at a function on Wednesday.
Asked whether there was a deadline for the rescue plan, he said the government, through its investment arm Khazanah Holdings Bhd, was given a period of time to study the proposal.
"It is not a deadline but a limited time for us to study (the proposal)," Mahathir said.
He said Khazanah was the only Malaysian company involved in the negotiations so far.
At another function, Deputy Prime Minister and Finance Minister Anwar Ibrahim told reporters the government has not made any commitment on the rescue plan.
"We are just looking at the proposal and we are negotiating. There is no firm commitment," Anwar was quoted as saying by New Straits Times daily.
The Asian Wall Street Journal on Wednesday reported that Malaysia is studying a rescue proposal with a group of international partners.
Malaysian government officials could not be immediately contacted for comment.
